title: Slow is smooth
summary: Play at a speed where nothing goes wrong, and let speed arrive on its own.
materials: the piece from your teacher, with a pencil

figure.alt: A bar of four steady clicks, one per beat. This stands for the metronome click you set to the slowest speed where the hard bars have no mistakes, before moving it up one notch at a time.

steps.title: Slow is smooth
steps.body:
Fingers learn whatever they repeat. Play a bar fast and wrong three times and you have practised the wrong notes three times. Play it slowly and right three times and you have practised the right ones.

So the rule this week is: choose a speed where nothing goes wrong. It will feel too slow. That is the point.

1. Put a metronome app on the phone. Find the slowest click at which you can play the hard bars with no mistakes.
2. Play them three times clean at that click.
3. Move the click up one notch, and only one. If a mistake comes back, go back down.
4. Finish with the whole piece once through, at the slow click.

Speed is not something you push. It arrives on its own once the notes are certain. By the fourth sitting you will be faster without having tried to be.

figure.alt: A bar of four steady clicks, the same click each sitting starts from. It moves up one notch only once the hard bars are clean three times in a row, and back down if a mistake returns.

steps.title: Four sittings
steps.body: Fifteen minutes each. Tick a sitting when it is done. Days do not matter; sittings do.
checklist: Sitting 1: find the no-mistake click for the hard bars, three clean times, then once through
Sitting 2: same bars, one notch up once they are clean three times
Sitting 3: one notch up again, back down if a slip comes back
Sitting 4: the whole piece at the slow click, then once through as if recording
Last week's piece, or any old piece, played once without the page

steps.title: Record this week's version
steps.prompt: Say the piece and the metronome number you ended on, then play it once through at that speed, hands in the frame.
